doc.title: Emile Barnes, George Guesnon, Little Brother Montgomery, Harold Dejan Interview, 1961-03-11

title: Recalling the 1936 hotel meeting and Guesnon's first record
summary: Guesnon recalls 1936 when he made his first record, 'Goodbye, Good Luck to You'; Montgomery says he had urged him, and Guesnon admits he feared recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, brother, I'm sure glad, let's bring back all the time, you know, the last time you and I sat down together was 1936, and we sat in the St. Shaw's Hotel, and I made my first sign of goodbye, good luck to you, you remember that?
Yeah, goodbye, good luck to you was a good number, I'd been trying to get you to make it all the time, but you scared, you know, you'd shy or something, I don't know...

Well, hell, I never made a record before, I thought making a record was like getting electrocuted and stuff, you know. Well, brother Montgomery, I'm glad you came now, and I'm glad to talk with you, I mean, and when you come down to town, you come down to New Orleans, I'll have this interview on tape. Well, so long, brother Montgomery.
